artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a locally finite graded poset with a unique minimal element 0̂, with rank function ρ : P → ℤ_{≥0} and rank sets P_n = ρ^{-1}(n). Let ℝP denote the free real vector space on P, and define the linear operators U, D : ℝP → ℝP by

  U(x) = Σ_{y ⋗ x} y,    D(x) = Σ_{y ⋖ x} y,

where ⋗ and ⋖ denote the covering relations in P. For a sequence of positive integers r = (r_0, r_1, r_2, …), call P an r-differential poset if

  DU − UD = r_n · I    on the subspace ℝP_n,    for every n ≥ 0.

It is known that for any such vector r there is at most one r-differential poset that is also a distributive lattice; denote it (when it exists) by L(r). It is also known that if the entries r_n grow "sufficiently fast" then L(r) exists.

Problem: Determine, in terms of an explicit growth condition on the sequence r = (r_n)_{n ≥ 0}, a sharp (necessary, and ideally also sufficient) rate of growth that characterizes the vectors r for which the r-differential distributive lattice L(r) exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Stanley's question on which vectors r admit an r-differential distributive lattice L(r) is widely regarded as hopeless in full generality; recent work (e.g., Worley 2026) extends the known construction to certain weighted-differential structures with positive weights and aims toward characterization, but no explicit description of the necessary rate of growth on r has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Constructing/analyzing differential distributed lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Restates and extends Stanley's technique; aims toward 'a complete characterization of distributive lattices with a weighted-differential structure with positive weights.'
status_evidence.claim: As of 2026, a full characterization (and hence the precise growth condition on r for L(r) to exist) is still being pursued, indicating the problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Differential poset — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Young's lattice is the only 1-differential distributive lattice; classification questions for general r remain active.
status_evidence.claim: General existence/growth criteria for r-differential distributive lattices are not known.
